description: Fly.io deployment config for wallabag, the self-hosted read-it-later app. Single app, SQLite, one volume, ~$2/mo.
readmeMarkdown:
# wallabag on Fly.io

Fly.io deployment config for [wallabag](https://github.com/wallabag/wallabag), a
self-hosted read-it-later app (save web pages, read them later, stripped of ads
and clutter).

Upstream ships a Docker image and a `docker-compose.yml`, but has no cloud
deployment guide. This runs it as **one Fly app** backed by **one volume**,
using SQLite:

| Fly app | image | exposure |
|---|---|---|
| `wallabag-af` | built from `wallabag/wallabag:2.6.14` + the `Dockerfile` here | **public** HTTPS, auto-suspend |

The container runs nginx + PHP-FPM under s6. Only port 80 is exposed; Fly
terminates TLS in front of it.

## ⚠️ Choose your own app name first

**Fly.io app names are globally unique** (shared across all Fly users). Plain
`wallabag` is confirmed taken — `fly apps create wallabag` returns
`Name has already been taken`. The name committed here is `wallabag-af`; pick
your own suffix.

Your instance is reachable at `https://<app-name>.fly.dev`, which is public and
the name is guessable — and wallabag ships with a **default `wallabag`/`wallabag`
login**. Pick something non-obvious *and* change the password immediately after
deploying (step 5 below).

If you change the name, update it in **both** places:

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| app name | `fly.toml` → `app` |
| public URL | `fly.toml` → `SYMFONY__ENV__DOMAIN_NAME` (`https://<app>.fly.dev`) |

Rename both at once (run in repo root, swap in your name):
```bash
sed -i "s|^app = 'wallabag-af'|app = 'YOUR-app'|; s|wallabag\.fly\.dev|YOUR-app.fly.dev|" fly.toml
```
Then use the same name in the `fly` commands below.

## Prerequisites
- [`fly` CLI](https://fly.io/docs/flyctl/install/) installed and `fly auth login` done
- `openssl` (for generating the secret)

## Cost (rough, LA region)

```
app machine (shared-cpu-1x 512mb, suspended when idle)   ≈ $1-2/mo
volume (1GB)                                             ≈ $0.15/mo
                                                         ──────────
                                                           ~$2/mo
```

Always-on instead is ≈ $3.47/mo for the machine — flip the two lines marked in
`fly.toml`'s `[http_service]` block. Reference prices: shared-cpu-1x 512mb
$3.32/mo always-on; volumes $0.15/GB/mo. A custom domain and its TLS cert are
free.

New Fly accounts have **no free tier** — this is pay-as-you-go.

## Deploy

### 1. Create the app
```bash
fly apps create wallabag-af        # use your own name; see above
```

### 2. Volume
```bash
fly volumes create wallabag_data --app wallabag-af --region lax --size 1
```

### 3. Secret
`SYMFONY__ENV__SECRET` signs CSRF tokens and remember-me cookies. The image
ships a hardcoded public default (`ovmpmAWXRCabNlMgzlzFXDYmCFfzGv`) — override
it before the first boot:
```bash
fly secrets set --app wallabag-af SYMFONY__ENV__SECRET="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
```

### 4. Deploy
```bash
fly deploy
fly logs --app wallabag-af
```
Watch for `Configuring the SQLite database ...` (first boot only) followed by
`wallabag is ready!`. First boot runs `wallabag:install` (4 steps) and then
`composer install` against the fresh volume — measured at **~30s** end to end on
a shared-cpu-1x.

`fly deploy` prints a warning as it finishes:

```
WARNING The app is not listening on the expected address ...
```

That is a race, not a failure — flyctl probes before the install finishes. Wait
for `wallabag is ready!` in the logs and it resolves on its own.

### 5. Change the default password — do this immediately
The instance is live at a public URL with the documented default login
`wallabag` / `wallabag`. Either change it in the web UI (**Config → Change
password**), or from the CLI:
```bash
fly ssh console --app wallabag-af \
  -C "php /var/www/wallabag/bin/console fos:user:change-password wallabag YOUR-NEW-PASSWORD --env=prod"
```

## Verify
1. `fly status --app wallabag-af` — machine `started`, health check passing (it may
   show `suspended` once idle; that's expected).
2. `curl https://wallabag-af.fly.dev/api/info` → JSON reporting version `2.6.14`.
3. Log in with the new password, save an article URL, confirm the content is
   fetched and readable.
4. `fly ssh console --app wallabag-af`, then:
   ```sh
   ls -la /var/www/wallabag/data/db/wallabag.sqlite   # non-empty (~221KB fresh)
   ls -ld /var/www/wallabag/web/assets/images         # symlink → /var/www/wallabag/data/images
   ```
5. `fly machine stop <id> --app wallabag-af`, then load the URL again → it resumes
   and the saved article is still there. Confirms the volume and auto-start path.
   Checking `stat -c '%i %s' .../wallabag.sqlite` before and after shows the same
   inode, which is the actual proof the volume persisted rather than a fresh DB.

## Ongoing
```bash
fly logs --app wallabag-af           # tail logs
fly status --app wallabag-af         # machine status
fly ssh console --app wallabag-af    # shell in
fly deploy                           # redeploy after a config or version change
```

Upgrading wallabag: bump the tag in `Dockerfile`, `fly deploy`, then run the
migration:
```bash
fly ssh console --app wallabag-af \
  -C "php /var/www/wallabag/bin/console doctrine:migrations:migrate --env=prod --no-interaction"
```

## Notes / gotchas

- **Why there's a Dockerfile.** A Fly Machine can mount only **one** volume, but
  wallabag wants two paths to persist: `data/` (the SQLite database) and
  `web/assets/images` (downloaded article images). The Dockerfile replaces the
  images directory with a symlink into `data/`, so one volume covers both.
  Without it, image downloads would silently vanish on every restart.

- **Why SQLite.** Postgres would mean a second, always-on Fly app (+$3.32/mo) for
  a single-user reading list. Upstream's entrypoint also creates the Postgres
  database as the superuser but never grants the app role rights on the `public`
  schema, which breaks first install on PostgreSQL 15+
  ([wallabag/docker#412](https://github.com/wallabag/docker/issues/412)). SQLite
  avoids both. If you outgrow it, wallabag supports migrating.

- **The volume mounts as `root`, wallabag runs as `nobody`.** Upstream's
  entrypoint only chowns `data/db`, so `fly-entrypoint.sh` creates and chowns
  the whole `data/` tree on every boot before handing off.

- **Downloaded images are opt-in.** wallabag only stores article images locally
  if you enable it in **Config → Settings**. They land on the volume via the
  symlink. Housekeeping:
  ```bash
  fly ssh console --app wallabag-af \
    -C "php /var/www/wallabag/bin/console wallabag:clean-downloaded-images --env=prod"
  ```

- **Suspend tears down long-running work.** Fly suspends the machine when the
  proxy sees no active connections. Run bulk imports from `fly ssh console`
  rather than leaving them to a background browser tab, or temporarily switch to
  the always-on values in `fly.toml`.

- **First boot vs the health check.** `grace_period` is set to 150s, which is
  deliberately generous — first boot measured ~30s. If the check ever flaps,
  check `fly logs` for `wallabag is ready!` before assuming a real failure.

- **Cold starts are slow-ish.** A request against a fully stopped machine
  measured **~21s** to return (image is 100MB and the entrypoint re-runs
  `composer install` on every boot). A `suspend`ed machine resumes much faster.
  If a 20s worst case bothers you, use the always-on values.

- **Memory.** 512mb + 512mb swap fits the install. If the first deploy OOMs,
  `fly scale memory 1024 --app wallabag-af`, let it finish, then scale back down.

- **One machine only.** A volume-attached app can't scale past a single machine,
  and deploys are not zero-downtime — Fly stops the old machine before starting
  the new one.

- **Email is not configured.** `SYMFONY__ENV__MAILER_DSN` defaults to
  `smtp://127.0.0.1`, and nothing listens there. Password-reset emails and
  email-based 2FA will not send. Set a real DSN (and
  `SYMFONY__ENV__FROM_EMAIL`) if you need them.

- **Custom domain** (optional, free): `fly certs add wallabag.example.com`, add
  the DNS records Fly prints, then update `SYMFONY__ENV__DOMAIN_NAME` in
  `fly.toml` and redeploy. Symfony builds absolute URLs from that value, so it
  must match the hostname you actually browse to.

- **Browser extensions and mobile apps** work against this instance via
  wallabag's API — create a client under **Config → API clients management**.
